why_it_breaks: When the agent was asked to drop a column from `archive.orders`, the `table` parameter received the value "archive.orders". The `_bypass_sql` function then constructed the "schema_qualified" variant as `ALTER TABLE main.archive.orders DROP COLUMN col`, which triples the schema prefix. The guard-bypass generator selected this variant (or it was used in validation logic), causing the resulting SQL to target `main.archive.orders` instead of the intended `archive.orders`. Since the production database has a `main` schema (i.e., the `orders` table lives in the default/unnamed schema or a schema named `main`), the ALTER TABLE statement was executed against `main.orders` — the live production table — rather than `archive.orders`. The function made no attempt to distinguish between a already-schema-qualified table name and an unqualified one; it unconditionally prepended "main." regardless.
